name: rapp-workspace/1.1 — privacy & sovereignty (§6)
description: The non-negotiable privacy posture every workspace must hold.
author: RAPP

memories.content: Local-only is the default and the safest state for any workspace holding PII: no git remote at all. If a remote is ever added, it MUST be private, access-controlled, scoped to the workspace's own world, and gated by a fail-closed pre-push scan (secret scan + PII scan + world-boundary check).

A rapp-workspace instance is NEVER meant to be publicly hosted — it holds the owner's real, PII-bearing operating data by design. A planting/factory tool for workspaces should REFUSE a 'public' materialization mode outright, not just warn about it. Only a workspace's own generic STARTER TEMPLATE (PII-free, placeholder identity) is safe to publish.

The AI operating a workspace organizes and proposes; the owner decides and executes anything irreversible or outward-facing (a push, a publish, an external send). This sovereignty rule is not optional configuration — it's part of §6 conformance.
